title: Europe’s Retirement Crisis Is an Opportunity for Insurers and Asset Managers
gist: A BCG survey of 6,000 consumers in France, Germany, Italy and Spain finds Europe's private retirement savings market is blocked not by affordability but by non-activation: only 54% of the target mass-affluent cohort even knows private pension solutions exist, and four out of five who ever discussed one had to initiate contact themselves. With EU public pension replacement rates falling from 45% to 41% by 2045 and regulatory unlocks landing in Germany (2027), Italy (2026) and Spain, the AuM pools (€1.54trn Germany, €317bn France, €243bn Italy, €163bn Spain) are up for recontest — and the under-35 cohort is already forming retirement decisions through GenAI rather than human advisors.

insights.claim: By 2045 Europe's ratio of working-age people to retirees will compress from roughly three workers per retiree today to fewer than two per retiree, mechanically undermining pay-as-you-go public pension systems.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The demand driver for private retirement products in Europe is not cyclical — it is a demographic ratio already fixed by births that have already happened; size the opportunity as secular, not macro-dependent.
insights.locator: Europe faces a retirement savings crisis hiding

insights.claim: The average replacement rate for earnings-related public pensions across the EU — the new pension as a share of average gross wage at retirement — will fall about 4 percentage points, from 45% in 2022 to 41% by 2045.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A quantified, quasi-certain 4pp income hole per retiree is the addressable revenue pool that private providers get to fill; it also sets the political ceiling on further public-pension generosity.
insights.locator: The Demographic Challenge

insights.claim: BCG frames Europe's pension shortfall as a certainty rather than a scenario, arguing the outcome follows from arithmetic rather than from forecasting assumptions.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Framing matters for underwriting: a thesis whose driver is arithmetic rather than a forecast justifies long-duration capital deployment into retirement distribution and platforms.
insights.quote: This is not a forecast. It is simple arithmetic.
insights.locator: Europe faces a retirement savings crisis hiding

insights.claim: Europe's public pension model is a pay-as-you-go structure in which today's workers fund today's retirees, so a shrinking workforce translates directly into lower benefits rather than into a funded asset shortfall that can be earned back through markets.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Because the mechanism is unfunded and demographic, market returns cannot rescue it — the adjustment must come through benefit cuts, higher contributions, or private substitution; only the third is investable.
insights.locator: The Demographic Challenge

themes.theme: EU Penetration Gap vs UK and US Benchmarks

insights.claim: Only 18% of European consumers own a personal pension product, according to the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
entities: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
insights.so_what: Penetration this low is the whitespace metric for European life insurers and asset managers — every 1pp of adoption is a multi-billion-euro flow event.
insights.locator: Yet few people in Europe have chosen

insights.claim: 44% of US households owned an individual retirement account as of mid-2024 according to the Investment Company Institute, roughly 2.4x the 18% personal-pension ownership rate in Europe.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The US ownership rate is the plausible convergence target for European penetration; it anchors how large the European fee pool could become if reform succeeds.
insights.locator: For its part, the US stands apart

insights.claim: The UK's headline statistic — just 16% of working-age adults actively contributed to a personal pension in 2023–2024 — understates its lead over the EU, because automatic enrollment launched in 2012 now covers about 80% of UK employees and has given the country the continent's deepest defined-contribution market.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Do not screen national pension markets on standalone personal-pension ownership; default-enrollment architecture is the variable that actually determines asset accumulation and where flows land.
insights.locator: Judging by these results, countries in the EU

insights.claim: In the UK, standalone personal pensions stayed small precisely because automatic enrollment absorbed the mass-market savings those products previously captured — a substitution effect, not weak demand.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Where auto-enrollment arrives in the EU, expect the value to shift from retail personal-pension distribution to workplace/occupational platform scale — position toward whoever runs the default.
insights.quote: Standalone personal pensions are modest precisely because automatic enrollment has absorbed the mass-market savings that such pensions once captured.
insights.locator: Judging by these results, countries in the EU

themes.theme: Country Reform Windows and AuM Pools

insights.claim: France's private retirement savings AuM stood at just €317 billion as of 2025 — €152 billion in individual plans and €165 billion in company-sponsored plans — after the 2019 loi PACTE consolidated products into the Plan d'Epargne Retraite and reignited inflows.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: France remains a small pool relative to its life insurance market, which is exactly why it carries the highest growth rate of the four — an underpenetrated base with a working policy catalyst.
insights.locator: Recent Reform Efforts

insights.claim: French private retirement savings AuM is estimated to grow around 7% annually through 2035, roughly double the projected growth rate of Italy or Spain and nearly triple Germany's.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: If you are picking one European retirement market for organic growth exposure, France offers the steepest compounding; Germany offers scale but low growth.
insights.locator: Recent Reform Efforts

insights.claim: Germany holds by far the largest European private retirement pool — €1.54 trillion of AuM as of 2024, split €1,064 billion individual and €475 billion company-sponsored — yet both segments are on track to grow only about 2.6% per year through 2035.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Germany is a share-shift market, not a growth market: returns there come from taking assets off incumbents, not from riding the pool's expansion.
insights.locator: Germany's retirement savings market is larger

insights.claim: Germany's Altersvorsorgereform, effective January 2027, removes the guaranteed capital maintenance requirement, shifting competition onto cost and performance and opening the market to asset managers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: This is a dated regulatory unlock on a €1.54trn pool: watch January 2027 as the entry point for low-cost asset managers and as a margin risk for German guarantee-based life insurers.
insights.quote: removing the guaranteed capital maintenance requirement, shifting competition onto cost and performance, and opening the market to asset managers
insights.locator: Germany's retirement savings market is larger

insights.claim: Italy's 2026 budget law tightens the pension opt-out window from six months to 60 days, extends the silent-assent auto-enrollment mechanism to job changers already enrolled in a fund, and — most substantively — makes employer contributions portable for the first time.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Portability converts captive employer-linked balances into contestable assets, which is how insurers and asset managers get to compete on cost and performance in Italy for the first time.
insights.quote: portable for the first time, a measure that could gradually open the market to asset managers and insurers competing on cost and performance.
insights.locator: Italy's retirement savings market has not seen

insights.claim: Italy has had auto-enrollment into supplementary pension funds via a silent assent mechanism since 2007, but successive governments made only incremental adjustments rather than structural reform, leaving total private retirement AuM at €243 billion as of 2024 (€99 billion individual, €144 billion company-sponsored).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Nearly two decades of auto-enrollment produced a pool one-sixth Germany's — evidence that default mechanics alone, without portability and competition, do not build scale.
insights.locator: Italy's retirement savings market has not seen

insights.claim: The retail-versus-occupational growth mix is inverted between Italy and Spain: Italian individual pension plans are projected to grow about 3.8% per year through 2035 against 2.0% for company-sponsored plans, while Spanish company-sponsored plans grow 4.2% against 3.0% for individual plans.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A pan-European retirement provider cannot run one channel strategy — Italy rewards retail distribution build-out while Spain rewards the workplace/occupational channel.
insights.locator: Italy's retirement savings market has not seen

insights.claim: Spain's Publicly Promoted Employment Pension Fund, created by Law 12/2022 alongside Simplified Occupational Pension Plans with the ambition of expanding occupational coverage from 2 million to 13 million workers by the end of the decade, has yet to attract any participants or assets and faces significant governance challenges.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A state-sponsored vehicle at literally zero assets against a 13-million-worker target is a cautionary read for anyone pricing in government-led pension expansion; the private simplified plans are the ones actually gaining traction.
insights.quote: the publicly promoted vehicle has yet to attract any participants or assets
insights.locator: Spain's private retirement savings market is the smallest

insights.claim: Spain has the smallest of the four markets at €163 billion of private retirement AuM as of 2025 (€122 billion individual, €41 billion company-sponsored), with individual plans heavily concentrated in bank distribution networks and occupational coverage restricted in practice to large companies.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Spanish banks control the retail retirement funnel, so insurers and asset managers entering Spain must either buy distribution or win the SME occupational segment that is currently unserved.
insights.locator: Spain's private retirement savings market is the smallest

insights.claim: Rising private retirement AuM across France, Germany, Italy and Spain would create a valuable pool of long-term capital available to support European economic growth, not just household income security.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Pension reform is also a European capital-markets-deepening trade: more domestic long-duration savings supports EU equity and infrastructure funding, a second-order beneficiary channel.
insights.locator: By encouraging people in France, Germany, Italy

insights.claim: 80% of surveyed Europeans with less than €250,000 in combined financial and real estate assets do not feel well-prepared for retirement — ranging from 76% in Germany to 83% in Spain — and nearly half of those with more than €250,000 share the same concern.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Anxiety is near-universal and cuts across wealth bands, so the constraint on product uptake is not affordability segmentation — it is reach.
insights.locator: The Opportunity

insights.claim: Among the mass-affluent core cohort that already holds savings accounts and life insurance at high rates, just 54% are aware that private retirement solutions exist, and fewer than 60% of those who are aware actually own one.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Roughly two-thirds of the most qualified prospects in Europe are lost to simple unawareness — a marketing and distribution problem with a much cheaper fix than product innovation.
insights.locator: At the same time, awareness of private pension

insights.claim: Once fully informed about the features private retirement plans offer, surveyed under-65s across France, Germany, Italy and Spain say they would raise their retirement savings allocation by an average of 10 percentage points.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 10pp allocation shift purely from information is the single largest quantified upside in the study — it makes customer education, not fee cuts, the highest-ROI lever for providers.
insights.locator: Once presented with the range of features

insights.claim: More than 90% of core-cohort respondents say they would welcome hearing from retirement planning advisors at certain life moments, yet more than four out of five who have ever discussed retirement products with an advisor had to initiate the contact themselves.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The gap between 90% receptivity and near-zero outbound is a pure execution failure by incumbent distributors — first mover on proactive outreach captures disproportionate share.
insights.locator: Clearly, there is considerable latent demand

insights.claim: The binding constraint on European private retirement uptake is the absence of communication between providers and consumers rather than any shortfall in consumer demand or capacity to save.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Underwrite European retirement plays on distribution intensity and outreach capability, not on product design or investment performance.
insights.quote: The demand is there, but the market is failing from lack of activation.
insights.locator: Yet private retirement savings—a source of income

insights.claim: Consumer interest in a private retirement product surges to over 70% the moment a product conversation is initiated, versus baseline ownership near 18% across Europe.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Conversion economics hinge almost entirely on conversation-initiation rate, which is a cost-to-serve and channel problem that AI-driven outreach can attack directly.
insights.quote: Interest surges to over 70% the moment a product conversation begins.
insights.locator: Conclusion

themes.theme: GenAI and Self-Direction Displacing Human Advisors

insights.claim: Two-thirds of surveyed Europeans seek retirement information on their own through online or AI research and 40% turn to friends and family, and both channels are strongly preferred over bank agents, insurance agents and tax advisors.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The traditional advice channel has already lost the top-of-funnel; whoever owns the AI answer layer for retirement questions owns the customer acquisition point.
insights.locator: What Do Consumers Want?

insights.claim: Among Europeans under 35, use of GenAI for retirement information already exceeds use of professional advisors, meaning the next generation forms its initial retirement decisions through AI and digital channels with no human advisor involved.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: This is a structural disintermediation signal for advisory-fee business models and a reason to value distribution embedded in AI surfaces over headcount-based advice networks.
insights.quote: the next generation is forming its initial retirement decisions through AI and digital channels without the involvement of human advisors
insights.locator: The shift is sharpest among those under 35

insights.claim: Around 65% of under-65 respondents in France, Italy and Spain prefer self-managed retirement savings options, rising to 77% in Germany.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Germany's 77% self-direction preference sits alongside its guarantee-heavy legacy product mix — a mismatch that the 2027 reform lets low-cost digital players exploit.
insights.locator: When it comes to retirement savings management

insights.claim: Despite the preference for self-management, 43% of younger European respondents want online solutions that include advice on demand, and almost 40% of 45-to-64-year-olds find advised or delegated solutions appealing.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The winning model is hybrid — self-serve rails with paid advice at moments of need — rather than either pure robo or pure advisor networks.
insights.locator: When it comes to retirement savings management

insights.claim: Only 12% of respondents report dissatisfaction with professional advisors, but among those the top complaint, cited by 40%, is perceived lack of impartiality — 15 percentage points above unclear explanation of options and 17 points above lack of listening.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Conflicted, commission-driven distribution is the specific trust failure to arbitrage; open-architecture or fee-based propositions have a defensible differentiation claim here.
insights.quote: The top reason for dissatisfaction, cited by 40%, is perceived lack of impartiality.
insights.locator: Respondents are equally clear about what they don’t want

insights.claim: More than one-third of surveyed Europeans say simulation and retirement planning tools would help them save more, with nearly as many pointing to pension estimators and automatic contribution systems calibrated to their bank balances.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Consumers are explicitly asking for behavioral-nudge software tied to bank data — a product spec for fintech partnerships and an argument for open-banking-linked savings automation.
insights.locator: When asked what support mechanisms would help

themes.theme: Decumulation, Protection and the Silver Economy

insights.claim: More than half of Europeans nearing retirement say they would be interested in advice on decumulation — how to withdraw funds from private plans after retiring — an underserved adjacency to accumulation products.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Decumulation advice is a fee pool available at the point of maximum account balance, and it is the mechanism for retaining assets that would otherwise leave the platform at retirement.
insights.locator: A Range of Opportunities

insights.claim: More than 45% of near-retirees express interest in supplementary health coverage, a figure that rises to 81% in France because of the structure of the French health insurance system.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: France is the standout cross-sell market for health and long-term-care attach at retirement — an 81% interest rate makes bundled propositions viable there before elsewhere.
insights.locator: A further key concern of those nearing retirement

insights.claim: Interest in retirement, savings and health offerings declines after people actually retire, with only half of retirees welcoming wealth management advice or ongoing financial guidance — ranging from 41% in Germany to 57% in Spain — probably because most have already fixed how they manage retirement income.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The acquisition window closes at retirement: providers who have not captured the relationship before the transition face a structurally less receptive customer afterwards.
insights.locator: Once retired, people's needs change

insights.claim: Retirees continue to spend even after they stop earning, opening partnership revenue across the silver economy from home-care services to senior living facilities and tourism platforms for older adults.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Pension providers hold decades-long trusted relationships with a high-net-spend cohort — that distribution asset is monetizable well beyond asset management fees.
insights.quote: Although retirees may be done earning, they are not done spending.
insights.locator: 4. Build on trust to support customers

themes.theme: Provider Playbook: Product Vendor to Life-Cycle Partner

insights.claim: BCG's four-step transformation for retirement providers runs from repositioning as a trusted retirement partner, to building a value-for-money proposition using AI, to delivering at the retirement transition, to capturing post-retirement value through decumulation, protection and silver-economy partnerships.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Use the four stages as a diligence checklist when assessing which European insurers and asset managers are actually repositioning versus merely relaunching products.
insights.locator: How Should Retirement Product Providers Respond?

insights.claim: The strategic prize in European retirement is framed as owning the customer relationship across a lifetime rather than filling a product gap, because the survey shows customers are anxious, poorly informed and hungry for guidance rather than short of suitable products.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Product-led entrants will underperform relationship-led incumbents in this market; assess competitors on engagement cadence and trigger-event outreach, not fund line-ups.
insights.quote: this is not a product gap to fill; it is a relationship to own
insights.locator: Conclusion

insights.claim: Retirement age is the point at which customers are simultaneously most anxious and most willing to pay for guidance, making it the moment to deploy human advisors and consolidation tools rather than spreading advisory capacity evenly across the life cycle.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Willingness-to-pay is time-concentrated, so advisor cost should be concentrated there too — a direct implication for cost-to-serve models and margin at retirement-transition cohorts.
insights.quote: Retirement age is the moment when customers are both most anxious and most willing to pay for guidance.
insights.locator: 3. Deliver value during the critical retirement transition

insights.claim: Because most Europeans' savings are fragmented across multiple accounts, plans and asset types, a provider that consolidates and simplifies a customer's financial life can win long-term trust and become the primary retirement partner.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Aggregation and consolidation tooling is the land-grab mechanism in this market — the same dynamic that let platform aggregators win in the UK and US retail retirement.
insights.quote: an insurer that can effectively simplify customers’ financial lives can earn their long-term trust and become their primary retirement partner
insights.locator: 3. Deliver value during the critical retirement transition

insights.claim: As AI-powered tools make it trivial for customers to compare providers on net-of-fee performance, advice impartiality and breadth of investment options, value for money becomes the primary competitive battleground — while AI simultaneously lowers providers' cost to serve through personalization and streamlined operations.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect fee compression in European retirement products alongside margin defense via AI-driven cost reduction; the spread between the two determines which providers survive the transition.
insights.locator: 2. Build a credible value-for-money proposition

insights.claim: Life events such as a promotion or an inheritance are identified as the specific triggers for reopening retirement income and tax optimization conversations, making event-driven outreach the practical mechanism for early customer engagement.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Providers with the data to detect life events — typically banks and bancassurers — have a structural advantage in the outreach game that decides this market.
insights.locator: 1. Reposition from savings provider to trusted retirement partner
